description: The fifteen OFFICIAL AI/Agent LEGO. This file is the single authoritative declaration of the AI/Agent LEGO set: every generated master document is produced from it. It declares responsibilities, boundaries and roadmap. It implements nothing.
setRule: These fifteen are official LEGO. They are not collapsed into one AI module, and no sixteenth top-level LEGO is created merely because a feature exists — a new feature is a sub-LEGO, a capability or an operation of an existing LEGO unless it owns a genuinely distinct lifecycle and data set.

statusVocabulary.implemented: Code exists, runs and is covered by tests.
statusVocabulary.contract-only: The contract is fixed and testable; no implementation exists.
statusVocabulary.planned: Intended; no contract is fixed yet.
statusVocabulary.blocked: Cannot proceed until a named blocker is resolved.
statusVocabulary.deferred: Deliberately postponed; no owner is scheduled.
statusVocabulary.in-progress: Implementation is underway; completion still requires reconciliation and protected-main verification.

conceptKinds.lego: A unit of ownership with its own contract, lifecycle, data and tests.
conceptKinds.sub-lego: A nested unit inside a LEGO. Reaching it requires an explicit declaration naming the child; nesting grants nothing.
conceptKinds.contract: The stable public surface. Lives above JS/Rust/WASM.
conceptKinds.provider: Where an implementation is sourced from.
conceptKinds.adapter: A translator at an edge between an external protocol and an internal contract.
conceptKinds.runtime: Where an agent or system executes.
conceptKinds.capability: An abstraction of WHAT can be done, independent of how.
conceptKinds.operation: One named, permissioned, interaction-classed action on a capability.
conceptKinds.ui-experience: A product surface rendered by the frontend. Not a LEGO.
conceptKinds.artifact: A referenced result. Never inlined into an event.
conceptKinds.event: A small, bounded record of something that happened.
conceptKinds.implementation: The swappable realisation of a contract.

architecture.rule: AI Foundation is the FOUNDATION, not the agent loop. It owns identity, policy binding, capability resolution and provider abstraction. The agent loop belongs to Agent Machine.
architecture.policyNote: `policy` in the chain is not a sixteenth LEGO. Policy binding is owned by AI Foundation and enforced at Capability and Approval; it is a responsibility, not a unit.

experiences.rule: Three product experiences over ONE AI Foundation. Three independent AI engines would triple the policy, capability and approval surface and guarantee they drift.

items.summary: Context-aware work assistant that narrows as the user focuses.
items.note: Execution AI is a Copilot MODE, not a separate engine. It is the same contracts with the scope narrowed to EXECUTION.

items.summary: AI as a workflow runtime component, executing inside a run.

lego.title: AI Foundation

reconciles.rule: Same unit. The official LEGO IS the existing core domain `ai-foundation`; this entry describes it, it does not create a second one.

lego.mission: Own the AI request lifecycle, AI identity, policy binding, capability resolution, provider abstraction and the shared AI contract surface.
lego.replacementBoundary: A provider is replaced by binding a different implementation to the same contract. No consumer changes.

lego.title: Skill
lego.mission: Package knowledge, rules, procedure and a capability map into a selectable, progressively disclosed unit.
lego.definition: Skill = knowledge + rules + procedure + capability map.

disclosureLevels.L0: identity — id, title, one line. Always cheap to list.
disclosureLevels.L1: card — when to use it, what it needs, what it produces.
disclosureLevels.L3: deep knowledge — references, examples, edge cases.

lego.disclosureRule: A skill is selected on L0/L1 and only then loaded deeper. Loading every skill's L3 into context is how a context window is exhausted before any work starts.
lego.replacementBoundary: A skill's procedure may be rewritten without changing its identity or card.
lego.versioningNote: Published in P2.12. The REGISTRY is implemented: registration, validation, lazy discovery and the six-state lifecycle are real, tested code declared as capability ai.skill on the ai-foundation domain. Skills remain declarative documents — nothing executes a procedure.
lego.phaseNote: Phase B, delivered in repository phase P2.12 — the skill registry only. Memory, Workspace and the agent loop remain planned.

lego.title: Agent Machine
lego.statusNote: P2.16 implements the bounded execution FOUNDATION of this LEGO as ai.agent-machine@1.1.0 (machine/agent/task identity, canonical agent lifecycle incl. ready, bounded step bookkeeping, budgets, registry-validated capability scope, bounded delegation bookkeeping, graph validation, event derivation, provider/executor seam). The loop, delegation execution, parallel runtime and fan-out/fan-in scheduling remain contract-only: this LEGO stays contract-only until the runtime is real.
lego.mission: Own the agent loop: agent and task lifecycle, delegation, parallelism and cancellation.
lego.authorityRule: Delegation NEVER implies permission inheritance. A child receives only an explicit subset of what the parent holds.
lego.replacementBoundary: A JS agent loop and a Rust agent loop satisfy the same contract. An external runtime satisfies it through Runtime Adapter.
lego.observability: agent.* and tool.* events; no reasoning.

lego.title: Memory
lego.mission: Own persistent knowledge as a traversable graph — not the current context window.
lego.distinction: Memory is persistent knowledge. Context is what is loaded right now. Conflating them produces a system that either forgets everything or loads everything.
nonScope: dumping full memory into a prompt
lego.loadRule: Never dump full memory into context. Load by graph traversal plus relevance, bounded by the caller's budget.
lego.providerNote: Obsidian is a Memory Provider / human knowledge interface adapter. It is NOT the internal source of truth, and the memory graph must remain valid with no provider connected.
lego.replacementBoundary: Graph storage may move from local JSON to SQLite to a graph store behind the same contract.
tests: test/lego-memory.test.mjs (create, recall, empty, invalid, duplicate, update, isolation, provider, integrity, forget, ordering, limits)
futureStages: relate: explicit edge creation as first-class operation
provider adapters: SQLite, filesystem snapshot, Obsidian projection as adapters
lego.phaseNote: P2.14 backend implementation: bounded local provider, scope-isolated retrieval, checksum lineage, explicit forget. No retrieval ranking, no embeddings, no vector store.
lego.statusNote: P2.14 implemented: memory survives context replacement, scope-isolated and provider-replaceable. Four operations only; traverse/relate deferred as future stages via explicit references.

lego.title: Workspace

reconciles.rule: Same unit. `workspace` is the existing core domain and P2.15 extends that domain with the bounded ai.workspace contract. There is no ai-workspace duplicate. Agent-1 owns the P2.15 implementation while Manager retains contract governance; Agent-2 remains frozen.

lego.mission: Own the explicit workspace identity and bounded logical lifecycle an agent may later act within; do not execute the action.
lego.scopingRule: Every operation names one workspaceId. The core uses exact identity lookup and never grants host-wide access, filesystem access or terminal access; future execution must consume this boundary through its own contract.
lego.replacementBoundary: InMemoryWorkspaceProvider is the default bounded provider; a replacement provider must preserve ai.workspace@1.0.0 and explicitly answer supports(kind). Provider durability and execution capabilities remain outside Workspace.
lego.observability: workspace identity/lifecycle transitions may be observed by the owning application; no provider internals, paths, commands or credentials are exposed.
lego.permissionRule: Read describes an exact identity. Create covers bounded lifecycle mutations. There is no ai:workspace:execute permission in P2.15.
lego.implementationBoundary: P2.15 implements identity, bounded metadata, opaque references, exact-id isolation, logical create/describe/mount/release and an explicit provider seam. It does not mount a filesystem or start a process.

lego.title: Context & Session
lego.mission: Own the distinction between conversation, session, context window, memory and execution — and manage rollover before a limit is hit.
lego.distinction: Conversation != Session != Context Window != Memory != Execution. One conversation may contain many sessions and many context windows.
lego.rolloverRule: Never wait for the exact context limit. Rollover is triggered at a declared threshold, because a rollover attempted at 100% has no room left to write the continuation package — the one operation that makes the rollover survivable.
lego.replacementBoundary: Compaction strategy is swappable behind the contract.
tests: planned: frontend/backend alignment and full reconciliation
lego.versioningNote: The contracts were conceptual in the P2.12 baseline. P2.13 publishes the smallest additive lock rows from the established fields and lifecycle vocabulary. The implementation is in-progress on the Agent 2 branch; Manager reconciliation is still required before milestone completion.
lego.phaseNote: P2.13 implementation milestone. Memory remains separate and follows this foundation.

lego.title: Universal Translation
lego.mission: Own translation, detection, localization and normalization as a capability — not merely a UI dictionary.
lego.localeNote: The locale baseline is a PLAN, not shipped support. Arabic is RTL, which is a layout concern the frontend owns; the backend owns the direction declaration.
lego.replacementBoundary: A model-backed translator and a dictionary translator satisfy the same contract.
tests: planned: markup preservation, RTL declaration, fallback when absent

lego.title: Node Creator

reconciles.rule: Node Creator is a sub-LEGO boundary of `node-registry` (owner agent-4), not a new top-level domain. The Node Contract it produces is already declared in manifest/node-contract.json.

lego.mission: Create and transform nodes through multiple declared strategies, each ending in conformance.
nonScope: choosing Rust for its own sake
lego.rustRule: Rust/WASM is one strategy among twelve. It must never be selected merely because it exists — only on measured benefit, and never requiring a compiler on an end-user device.
lego.replacementBoundary: Each strategy is an implementation of one creation contract.

lego.title: Capability

reconciles.rule: Same mechanism. The official Capability LEGO is the existing capability/negotiation infrastructure owned by `lego-foundation` (contracts lego.domain-registry, lego.negotiation). No parallel AI capability registry is created.

lego.mission: Own the abstraction that separates WHAT can be done from HOW and WHERE it is done.
lego.distinction: Capability != tool implementation. `filesystem.write` is one capability with many possible implementations: native, container, remote worker, MCP, external runtime.
lego.classRule: Exactly four interaction classes. No internal fifth class may be added.
lego.countCorrection: P2.10 prose and its evidence file stated 173 operations. The manifest has always declared 139 (82 capabilities, 62 of which declare operations); the 173 figure was an arithmetic error, not a change in the data. `manifest/domains.json` is byte-identical to its P2.10 state. The count is now generated rather than written, so it cannot drift again.

lego.title: MCP Adapter
lego.mission: Translate between MCP and internal capability contracts at the edge.
lego.boundaryRule: MCP maps ONTO the tool gateway; the tool gateway is not defined in MCP terms. If MCP changes, one adapter changes.
lego.internalRule: No internal LEGO may call another over MCP. Native capabilities use native contracts.
lego.discoveryRule: Controlled discovery with lazy loading. Never load hundreds of external tools into context by default — tool descriptions are context, and an unbounded tool list exhausts the window before any work begins.
lego.replacementBoundary: The adapter is replaceable; the tool gateway contract is not affected.
tests: planned: adapter conformance, lazy discovery bounds
lego.versioningNote: The tool-gateway contract it binds to is published at 1.0.0; the adapter contract itself is unpublished.
lego.statusNote: P2.20 publishes ai.mcp-boundary@1.0.0: the four-state MCP boundary declaration (declared / permission-required / exposed / blocked) with an explicit permission gate, fail-closed unknown-server/capability/permission handling and strict authority separation from Agent Control, in src/lego/mcp-boundary.mjs. The LEGO stays contract-only: no MCP server, no MCP client, no adapter runtime, no SDK and no network — adapter implementation stays P3/FUTURE.

lego.title: Runtime Adapter
lego.mission: Let an external agent runtime participate through one canonical lifecycle.
lego.noRewriteRule: External runtimes are NEVER reimplemented — in Rust or otherwise. They are adapted. Reimplementing a third-party agent harness means owning its bugs and its release cycle for no architectural gain.
lego.replacementBoundary: Every runtime is one implementation of ai.agent-runtime.
lego.statusNote: P2.21 publishes ai.runtime-adapter@1.0.0: the contract-preserving adapter seam (explicit provider registration, EXTERNAL executorKind fail-closed without an eligible provider, lifecycle translation onto ai.agent-machine@1.1.0) plus a deterministic in-process/simulated harness, in src/lego/runtime-adapter.mjs. The LEGO stays contract-only: no external runtime is implemented, nothing is rewritten — external runtimes are adapted, never reimplemented. ai.agent-runtime stays the lifecycle contract; no MCP, no model, no scheduler, no shell/filesystem authority.

lego.title: Artifact
lego.statusNote: P2.19 implements the bounded ai.artifact@1.0.0 foundation (opaque reference-only identity, sha256 integrity semantics, lifecycle, secret-safe bounded metadata) in src/lego/artifact.mjs. The LEGO stays contract-only: no storage engine and no filesystem authority — storage providers remain contract-only.
lego.mission: Hold results by reference, with checksum and retention.
lego.referenceRule: Artifacts are referenced, never inlined. A giant payload inside an event makes every consumer of that event pay for data it usually does not read.
lego.replacementBoundary: storageRef is opaque: local file, SQLite row or object store.

lego.title: Approval
lego.statusNote: P2.19 implements the bounded ai.approval@1.0.0 foundation (request/grant/deny with required scope, fail-closed evaluation, deterministic duplicates, expiration and the dependency-side waiting resolution for Agent Machine approvalReferences) in src/lego/approval.mjs. The LEGO stays contract-only: no approval UI, no executor, no enforcement middleware.
lego.mission: Be the formal control boundary for consequential actions.
nonScope: deciding policy for a domain it does not own
lego.failClosedRule: Unknown and destructive actions FAIL CLOSED. An expired or unanswered approval is a DENY. Read-only must be proven, never assumed — the tempting `list.includes(action)` implementation returns false for anything new, so a newly added destructive action would need no approval until someone remembered to extend the list.
lego.authorityRule: Child agents never inherit authority automatically.
lego.replacementBoundary: Policy engine swappable behind the contract.

lego.title: Agent Event & Work Trace
lego.mission: Record operational activity in small, bounded, reference-based events.
lego.privacyRule: Work Trace represents operational activity, NOT private reasoning. Chain-of-thought is never stored: it is not an audit format, and retaining it creates a liability with no operational benefit.
lego.replacementBoundary: Event sink swappable; vocabulary is not.
lego.observability: this LEGO IS the observability surface for AI.

lego.title: Token & Usage
lego.mission: Account for token and resource usage honestly, distinguishing reported from estimated.
lego.honestyRule: Never fabricate provider metrics. A token count that the provider did not report is `estimated` and must be labelled as such — an estimate presented as a measurement is worse than no number, because it cannot be audited.
lego.uiRule: Message text stays dominant; per-message token metadata stays subtle (e.g. `· 8 tokens`). A detailed view may expose message/context/output/total/source. Context-level usage may show e.g. `Context 61%`.
lego.uiOwner: agent-1 owns the rendering; this LEGO owns the numbers and their provenance.
tests: test/lego-token-usage.test.mjs (record provenance, zero-vs-unavailable, estimator identity, idempotent requestId, budget derivation, cost pricing basis, secret/content refusal)
planned: UI surface (agent-1), provider-reported metrics (stage E)

externalActionModel.rule: Every external action routes through Capability + Policy + Workspace. An agent never receives unrestricted OS authority by default.
externalActionModel.status: contract-only — none of these capabilities is implemented

CORE.summary: n8n alone. No AI provider configured.
CORE.note: This is the zero-install state and it is fully supported.

REMOTE_AI.summary: n8n plus a remote model provider.

CONNECTED.summary: n8n plus remote model and tool/application providers.

POWER.summary: n8n plus local and remote runtimes, workspaces and providers.

deploymentModes.rule: Zero-install must work with no inference provider. The system reports 'AI foundation ready, no inference provider configured' and never fakes a completion.

performanceRules: Direct local dispatch for same-process calls.
Zero internal HTTP between local LEGO.
No broker for simple local interactions.
No full transcript held in hot RAM.
MCP and tool loading are lazy.
Boot stays lightweight; no AI code loads unless used.
Use a transport only when a real boundary requires one.
securityInvariants: A child or nested LEGO does not inherit authority automatically.
A vendor adapter cannot silently become a business contract.
A destructive or unknown action requires explicit policy resolution.
Approval semantics are explicit, never implied.

rustStrategy.rule: Rust is not a goal. It is a measured implementation choice behind a stable contract.
rustStrategy.candidateRule: These are n8n-CONTROLLED components where the workload is hot, long-lived and measurable. A candidate is only migrated after measurement, never on principle.
rustStrategy.neverRewriteReason: Reimplementing a third-party agent harness means owning its bugs and release cycle for no architectural gain. They are adapted through Runtime Adapter.
rustStrategy.contractRule: Every JS -> Rust replacement stays behind a stable contract and changes no consumer.

B.title: Skill / Memory / Workspace / Agent Machine
delivered: skill registry (P2.12): registration, validation, lazy discovery, lifecycle
Context & Session foundation implementation target (P2.13): bounded lifecycle and continuation mechanics

D.title: Work Trace / Node Creator / Translation / Token

F.title: Native agent execution and measured optimisation

phases.rule: No phase may silently skip contract compatibility. A phase that needs a contract change declares it, versions it and migrates consumers.

currentLimits: AI runtime is NOT implemented: no model inference, provider API calls, Agent Machine loop or multi-agent runtime.
Model inference is NOT implemented; no provider API calls are made.
Memory persistent store remains NOT IMPLEMENTED; Context is what is loaded now and Memory is what survives replacement.
Workspace runtime, MCP runtime, Runtime Adapter runtime, Node Creator runtime and Translation runtime remain NOT IMPLEMENTED.
Rust is ACTIVE (PHASE 3): 8 workspace crates under crates/, cargo workspace green as of main f63a91e7. The backend is NOT scale-out ready; scale-out remains NOT READY.
Next implementation milestone is NOT AUTHORIZED after P2.27 + P3/P4/P6/P9 integration; P2.17+ is an umbrella planning bucket only (Issue #81 stop rule).
reconciliationRule: A LEGO in this set whose id collides with, or whose mechanism is already owned by, a core domain in manifest/domains.json MUST declare `reconciles`. This is what stops the AI set from silently forking a second domain (ai-workspace beside workspace, an AI capability registry beside lego-foundation). Gate rule F17 enforces it.
phaseDependencyRule: A LEGO must not depend on a LEGO scheduled in a later phase, because a roadmap that cannot run in its own stated order is not a roadmap. Exceptions are declared below with the degradation that makes the earlier phase viable on its own — never left implicit.

phaseDependencyExceptions.why: The phase split places Agent Machine in B and Approval in C, so the agent loop is built before the approval LEGO exists. This is deliberate and safe ONLY because approval fails closed: with no Approval LEGO present, any action whose approval requirement is unknown or destructive is refused, not permitted. Phase B therefore ships an Agent Machine that can orchestrate read-only and explicitly-safe work and refuses the rest.
phaseDependencyExceptions.degradation: Without approval: `lego.access_denied` on any action requiring or of unknown approval status.
phaseDependencyExceptions.closes: Phase C, when ai.approval is published.
